title: Trump to unveil $2.4B in AI credits to boost federal research
excerpt: Nvidia, AMD, OpenAI, Anthropic and Google are donating $2.4B to the Genesis Mission. Three of the five were named by Britain's regulator that morning.
content_html:
Five American technology companies are pledging $2.4B in AI tools and compute credits to federal science at a White House summit, with Nvidia giving $1B and Google the smallest share at $150M. The same administration suspended Microsoft from a residency programme hours earlier, and Britain’s regulator named three of the five donors that morning.

Five American technology companies are pledging $2.4B to federal science. Nvidia is giving $1B, AMD $500M, OpenAI $200M, and Anthropic and Google $150M each. The money takes the form of AI tools and compute credits for the Genesis Mission.

Trump announces it on Thursday at a Washington summit called Science: A New Golden Age, which also carries more than $100M for science and engineering education. Musk, Jensen Huang, Sergey Brin and Lisa Su receive the National Medal of Science there, and Michael Dell the National Medal of Technology and Innovation, Bloomberg reported.

Michael Kratsios, the White House science policy director, said the commitments would channel billions across the science ecosystem. Nvidia announced its own share earlier in the day, spread over five years across university research, quantum computing and cloud providers serving government.

One guest had a complicated morning.

Satya Nadella is being honoured at the summit. Hours earlier the vice president and the labor secretary suspended Microsoft from the programme that lets employers sponsor foreign staff for permanent residency, alongside Adobe and six IT services firms, citing alleged fraud. Capgemini, the one European name on that list, was not invited to Washington.

Nobody has explained how the compute gets reserved.

Credits are not capacity, and the companies issuing them are selling the same machine time to customers paying commercial rates. It is unclear how the pledged power will be set aside for scientists, Bloomberg noted.

Britain spent the same morning on the same companies.

The Information Commissioner’s Office named Google, OpenAI and Anthropic among ten developers it had secured changes from after two years of scrutiny, and opened a call for evidence on how organisations manage the risks from AI agents.

Three of the five donors, in other words.

Trump has called AI safety concerns a hoax. Last week he and a group of AI executives signed an accord with no mandatory guardrails, under which companies would work with outside auditors and tighten their own internal controls.

The Genesis Mission already had money.

We reported in July that it had more than $5B behind it across fifteen agencies. What it did not have, and still does not, is a guaranteed place in the queue for machines.
